fatal_errors: The proposed material, processing intervention, comparator, and test electrolyte do not reconstruct the target study: SPS MgAlTiVFeCo at different sintering temperatures in NaCl replaces as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 versus thermally shocked DS2205 in deionized-water tribocorrosion.

The cited evidence supports corrosion resistance, density, and hardness but does not establish simultaneous wear-corrosion performance, reduced tribocorrosion synergy, or mechanical persistence of the proposed spinel film.

Changing sintering temperature also changes densification, hardness, porosity, and potentially bulk phases, so the proposed comparison cannot attribute improved behavior specifically to the oxide film.
The experiment lacks corrosion-only and wear-only controls needed to calculate or test the claimed reduction in wear-corrosion synergy.
explanation: This is a coherent and testable alternative hypothesis centered on a hard protective oxide, and its oxygen availability and film-removal boundaries are sensible. It nevertheless has little agreement with the hidden target, whose key mechanism is temperature-dependent competition between depassivation, repassivation, and tribolayer disruption in a stable L12/B2 lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy relative to DS2205. The target also predicts a nonmonotonic minimum near 50 °C, whereas the generated answer treats higher processing temperature as monotonically beneficial. The proposed electrochemical and wear measurements could establish a performance difference, but they would not isolate the oxide mechanism from sintering-induced density and microstructural changes. Direct film composition/thickness measurements, oxide-removal or preoxidation controls, matched-density specimens, and separate wear-only and corrosion-only arms would be required. Evidence E1 is relevant to corrosion and hardness but is insufficient support for the central tribocorrosion claim.
